facts.text: Clarkston, officially the City of the Village of Clarkston, is a small city in Oakland County that is surrounded by Independence Township but has been administered independently since it incorporated as a city in 1992.
With about 0.44 square miles of land, Clarkston is the smallest city by land area in Michigan.
Main Street through downtown Clarkston is M-15.

The Clarkston Village Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, includes more than 100 historic structures on streets such as Main, Depot, Church, Buffalo and Washington, among them many preserved Queen Anne style homes.
Clarkston has a Historic District Commission, and the city provides a work permit application for projects within the Clarkston Historic District.
Depot Park, at the City Hall address of 375 Depot Road, has a rentable gazebo, a playground, picnic areas and a bike trail.

Clarkston High School's Team RUSH 27 robotics team has organized the Clarkston Holiday Lights Parade, an annual winter parade of lighted floats, since 2001; the 2026 parade is scheduled for December 12 at 6 p.m.
Independence Township, which surrounds Clarkston, is home to Pine Knob Music Theatre and the Pine Knob ski resort.
After I-75 came through Independence Township in 1962, many of its farms gave way to subdivisions and strip malls.
The Clinton River winds through Independence Township, which has more than thirty named lakes of all sizes.

hub.intro: Clarkston fits a historic village into less than half a square mile. Homes and businesses in the village, and in the Independence Township neighborhoods around it, are within our service area for the whole season: design, installation, in-season service and removal. Elevated work is done from bucket trucks, and every estimate is free.
hub.local_context: The City of the Village of Clarkston has been administered as its own city since 1992, even though Independence Township surrounds it. Its heart is the Clarkston Village Historic District, placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, with more than 100 historic structures and many preserved Queen Anne homes along streets like Main, Depot, Church, Buffalo and Washington. Outside the village the setting changes. Subdivisions and strip malls replaced many farms after I-75 came through in 1962, and the township holds more than thirty named lakes. Each of those settings calls for its own lighting plan, from detailed porch trim to long suburban rooflines and houses that face the water.
highlights: Queen Anne porches and gables in the village, plus subdivision homes across the township, lit for Christmas
Storefront, building and tree lighting for businesses on Main Street (M-15), township strip malls and HOA entrances
Year-round, app-controlled roofline lighting, planned with the historic district in mind

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Clarkston, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Clarkston, MI Christmas light installation for Queen Anne porches in the village and subdivision rooflines in the township. Full service, free estimate.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Clarkston, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Queen Anne porches, gables and subdivision rooflines, lit in clean lines by bucket-truck crews, kept glowing all season and removed once the holidays end.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Clarkston is a small place with a lot of trim. The Clarkston Village Historic District holds more than 100 historic structures, and many are preserved Queen Anne homes with porches, gables and layered rooflines. Lighting a house like that well means following the architecture: outlining the main gables, running the porch rail and fastening with care on older wood. Subdivision homes in the surrounding Independence Township usually call for a different plan, with longer eaves, garage peaks and yard trees worth wrapping. We design for the house you actually have, send bucket-truck crews for the high runs, keep the display working through the season and take it all down after the holidays.
considerations: Queen Anne homes reward restraint. One warm line along the main gables and the porch usually reads better than lights on every edge. We map each run around turned posts, brackets and shingle work, so the house still looks like itself after dark, only brighter.

Clarkston has a Historic District Commission, and the city provides a work permit application for projects inside the district. If your home is inside the district and you are unsure whether anything applies to seasonal lighting, a call to City Hall before install day is the simplest way to find out. We can share the design plan for that conversation.

Team RUSH 27, the Clarkston High School robotics team, has run the Clarkston Holiday Lights Parade since 2001, and the 2026 parade is set for December 12. If you want your house lit well before then, ask early. Install dates commonly fall between October and early December, and early requests see more open dates.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights in Clarkston and Independence Township?

Yes. The village and the township around it both sit inside our Southeast Michigan service area, which centers on Oakland, Genesee and Livingston counties. Include your address when you request an estimate so the design can be planned around your home, your trees and your lot.
What will my Clarkston estimate cover?

It covers the design and everything that follows. We note which rooflines, porches, trees and shrubs to light, then lay out installation, service while the lights are up and takedown after the holidays. The estimate spells out exactly what is included, so you can read the scope line by line before deciding.
When do the lights come down?

After the holidays. Takedown is part of full service, along with design, installation and upkeep while the display is up. Crews take each run down with the same care used to put it up, which matters on older trim and porch rails, and they leave the property tidy.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Clarkston, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Holiday displays for Main Street storefronts, Independence Township strip malls and HOA entrances in Clarkston, MI. Designed, installed and removed.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Clarkston, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Storefront outlines, wrapped trees and entrance displays for Clarkston businesses, property managers and HOAs, installed and removed by crews with bucket trucks.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Clarkston is compact, and that works in a business's favor during the holidays. Main Street doubles as M-15, so through traffic passes historic storefronts at close range, and a clean building outline or a pair of wrapped trees gets noticed. Out in Independence Township, the strip malls that followed I-75 need lighting that reads from a moving car and from the parking lot at dusk. Subdivision and HOA entrances are their own category, where a lit sign bed and two flanking evergreens can welcome residents home all season. Whatever the property, the plan covers the whole season: design, installation (with bucket trucks for anything tall), service during the season and removal after the holidays.
considerations: Many buildings along Main Street sit inside the Clarkston Village Historic District. Fastening points and fixture placement are planned with that in mind, and we recommend confirming with the city whether its historic district work permit applies to your display before the install is scheduled.

Drivers on Main Street pass by quickly, so a display needs a strong, simple shape. Rooflines, window frames and one or two wrapped trees beat scattered decorations almost every time. We aim the design at two views: the one from the road and the one from the sidewalk.

Strip mall owners and HOA boards across Independence Township often look after several signs, poles and landscape beds. One plan can cover an entrance, a sign island or a full row of storefronts, with a single estimate that lists every element included.
faq: Can you light Clarkston businesses and managed properties?

Yes. Businesses, shopping centers, HOAs, condo associations and property managers across Southeast Michigan can request commercial holiday lighting, and Clarkston and Independence Township are part of that area. If the building sits inside the historic district, mention it in your request so the plan accounts for it from the start.
When should a Clarkston business book holiday lighting?

Sooner is better. Commercial work generally goes up between October and early December, and the first requests have the most date options. If you want the storefront lit before the Clarkston Holiday Lights Parade in December, reach out while the fall calendar is still open.
Does the estimate include service during the season and removal?

Full service here means we design it, install it, keep it running until the holidays are over and then remove it, and your estimate lists what that covers for your property. If a section goes dark mid-season, a call to (248) 756-8915 puts a crew visit on the schedule.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Clarkston, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Clarkston permanent Christmas lights for village Queen Anne homes and Independence Township lake houses: mounted once, run from an app. Free estimate.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Mounted once along the eaves of a village Queen Anne or a township lake house, then set from your phone for December, a summer evening or any night in between.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Some Clarkston rooflines take real effort to relight every fall. A Queen Anne home in the historic district can have several roof planes and layered trim, and a long subdivision roofline in Independence Township means a lot of ladder work each season. Permanent lighting mounts along the eaves once, stays there and runs from your phone. The same lights can glow warm white over a summer dinner on the porch, then switch to red and green when December arrives. Before anything is mounted, the estimate shows every section of the roofline it covers.
considerations: Permanent lighting stays attached to the house, which is a different question from seasonal clips. If your home is in the Clarkston Village Historic District, ask the city's Historic District Commission about the work permit application first. Our design plan shows exactly where the lighting would run.

Independence Township has more than thirty named lakes, and a home on one of them has two fronts. We plan the layout for how the house looks from the shoreline as well as the street, so the lakeside eaves never feel like an afterthought.

The same lights handle Christmas, the Fourth of July, a birthday or a quiet glow on a January evening. Settings live in an app, so changing the look takes a few taps instead of an afternoon on a ladder.
faq: Is permanent lighting available in Clarkston?

Yes, in the village and across Independence Township. It suits Queen Anne houses near Main Street as well as newer homes in township subdivisions and houses on the lakes. Tell us which parts of the roofline you see most, and the free estimate lists each run it covers.
Does permanent lighting suit an older home in the village?

It can, with the right plan. Houses of that age often have complex trim and several roof planes, so we map the runs to the lines that define the house and choose mounting points that suit older wood. You see the full layout on the estimate before any work is scheduled.
Can I add tree wraps in December?

Yes. The permanent run covers the roofline, and seasonal tree wraps, shrub lighting or a lit entry can go up alongside it each December. We install both, so one estimate can cover a permanent roofline and a seasonal display for the yard.
